newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia beef prices seen higher in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia beef prices seen higher in 1997/98.

text.p: Australian beef saleyard prices are expected to increase to average 170 cents a kg in 1997/98 (July/June) after averaging 150 cents a kg in 1996/97, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.

ABARE, the Australian government's main commodities forecasting agency, said the expected improvement in 1997/98 was mainly due to an anticipated tightening of beef supplies in the United States and a recovery in beef import demand in South Korea and Japan.
However, uncertainty over developments in Australia's export markets and the Australian dollar's exchange rate could reduce the average price in 1997/98 to between 146 and 182 cents a kg.
In its latest Australian Commodities bulletin, ABARE said Australian beef exports to the United States are forecast to increaes by almost three percent in 1997/98.

Australian exports to Japan were forecast to increase by four percent in 1997/98 in response to increased demand for imported beef as Japanese consumer concerns over mad cow disease and E.Coli recede.
Australian exports to South Korea were forecast to increase in 1997/98 to meet the rising domestic demand for beef.

ABARE said Australian live cattle exports were growing strongly, reflecting strongly demand from Southeast Asia for feeder cattle. Australian live cattle exports were forecast to rise to 770,000 in 1997/98 from 735,000 in 1996/97.
"The reimposition of bans by Egypt and Libya on live cattle imports from Ireland, France and Portugal will increase opportunities for Australian exports to those markets," ABARE said.
